summary: Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was a scholar in archaeology, history, and Indology. He was a professor at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (~1964–1995) and director of the editorial committee at the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente (~1995–2000).

Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," worked as a researcher at the University of Hamburg (1990), and held posts at IsIAO and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018).

Mavis L. Fenn studied English at the University of Winnipeg, religious studies at the University of Calgary, and completed a PhD under Graeme MacQueen at McMaster University. She held positions at United College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Deeg is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021).

Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University (~1889–1891) and later held posts there (~1891–1892), at the University of California, Berkeley (~1897–1905), and at Dropsie College (~1909–1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indologist who completed his studies under Ernst Windisch at Leipzig University in 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a historian of Tibet and China. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark C. Elliott (~2007–2014), later holding a post at Georgetown University (~2013).

Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Heidelberg University (~1902–1938) and founded both the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde.
Maxime Kaltenmark (1910–2002) was a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1979) and the University of Paris (~1957–1979).
McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott (1924–2024) was an anthropologist and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1947–1953) and served there as a professor of anthropology and social sciences from ~1953 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, PGIPBS, and Nanjing University, later holding posts at the University of Colombo (~2004), Buddhist and Pali University (2008), and PGIPBS (2008).
Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).
Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009), where she studied under Dieter Schuh and doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger.
Meiji Yamada is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He also served as a professor there (attested 1963, 2007).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

Melissa R. Kerin specializes in art history, archaeology, and Buddhist and Tibetan studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and joined Washington and Lee University as a professor (attested 2015).

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington (PhD 1960–1968), and became a professor at Case Western Reserve University around 1968.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn A. A. Cissell.
